items.source: frozen per-item lane banks, dataset csoai/gspc-peritem-rows-2026-08-12 (the same files ci/frontier-runner.py reads)
items.selection_rule: sort the lane's (item, gold) pairs by sha256(lane + NUL + item_text) ascending, take the first items_per_lane
items.grader: harness/gspc-top100/mill_hub_queue.py::read_label; an answer that is not one menu label is the category UNPARSED, which counts as its own category
items.item_visibility: PUBLIC_BANK (the held-out question is open, see HELDOUT-DESIGN.md)

call_rules.order: all (item, repeat) calls of one batch shuffled together with a seeded RNG, so time of day is spread across items

declared_sampling.seed: unset unless the provider requires one

call_rules.system_prompt: none (calibration condition C3 changes it on purpose)

statistic.name: mean_tv_permutation
statistic.definition: for item i let p_i and q_i be the share of each answer category in the baseline batch and the new batch; TV_i = 0.5 * sum_c |p_ic - q_ic|; T = mean over items of TV_i
statistic.null: within each item, pool the 2K answers and re-split them at random into K and K; recompute T
statistic.p_value: (1 + number of permuted T >= observed T) / (1 + b)
statistic.rng_seed_rule: integer from sha256(protocol_id + comparison_id), so a comparison can be recomputed byte for byte

flag_rule.meaning: the answer distribution on the probe items moved against the baseline by more than the model's own run-to-run spread. It says THAT behaviour moved on these items. It does not say why, where, or whether it matters.

baseline.first_run_for_a_model: writes the baseline (K repeats), compares nothing, state BASELINE_SET
baseline.replacement: never automatic; only by a person starting the workflow with rebaseline=true, which records the hash of the baseline it replaces
baseline.signed: digest record signed in GitHub Actions only

calibration.model_family: one open model, size chosen so the run fits free compute; exact repo, revision and file hashes are written to calibration-pins.json and committed BEFORE any calibration run

C1.name: different revision of the same model

C2.name: quantised copy of the same revision

C3.name: changed system prompt (one added neutral sentence, text fixed in calibration-pins.json)

calibration.trial: one full batch (all items x K repeats) under the condition, compared to the one baseline batch with the unchanged statistic and flag rule
calibration.reported: for each condition: flags / trials with an exact 95% (Wilson) interval, plus mean T. C0 is the false-flag rate; C1 to C4 are the detection rates. Every condition is reported, including those that go badly.
calibration.synthetic_checks: unit tests with planted and unplanted synthetic data prove the code, not the method. They are never reported as calibration.

enable_conditions: a named person has confirmed, per provider, that the governing agreement permits benchmarking and publishing the result; recorded in scripts/silent-change/paid_models.json as confirmed_by_person and confirmed_on
C0 false-flag rate has been measured and published beside the watch
watch.schedule: one batch per model per day at a random minute inside a fixed window
watch.publication: a flag is printed with the calibration rates beside it. It is never labelled a cause, a degradation, or a safety verdict. Own-council models are never ranked publicly; the watch has no ranking at all.
watch.multiplicity: no correction across models, banks and days is applied. The expected number of false flags per day is models x C0 rate and is stated beside every report.

not_done_by_this_protocol: weights, raw reasoning and training data of paid models (stay in unmeasured[])
any claim about items outside the probe items
any comparison of one model with another

addendum_1.data_quality_gate: if more than 5 percent of the calls of a batch fail at the transport (network error, timeout, HTTP error other than a refusal of credentials), the batch is UNCHECKABLE: it is not compared, not counted as a flag and not counted in any rate. A failed fetch is never read as 'unchanged' or 'changed'. UNPARSED answers are not transport failures; they stay a category.

addendum_2.scope: calibration run on free GitHub-hosted runners; sections 1 to 6 and the statistic, the flag rule and addendum_1 are unchanged

open_model.family: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct GGUF (Apache-2.0), served by llama.cpp release b12651 llama-server on the runner
open_model.server: one serial request at a time, prompt cache off (cache_prompt false), context 2048, a fixed server seed per shard, the model's own chat template; no other sampling setting is changed

BASE.role: the one baseline batch for C0 to C4

C1.change: a sibling model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, same Q8_0 quantisation). Replaces 'a different revision of the same model': the 0.5B GGUF files have the same sha256 in every revision of their repository (checked 23 Nov for the first and the second commit), so no different revision exists to run.

C2.change: the same weights quantised Q4_K_M instead of Q8_0

C3.system: Read the question carefully before answering.

BASE5.role: the one baseline batch for C5

C5.change: none: the no-change control while the model is sampling, compared with BASE5

addendum_2.why_c5: At temperature 0 on a serial local server the same file is expected to repeat its answers, so C0 may show exactly no movement and then says little about false flags under run-to-run noise. C5 is the same no-change test while answers vary. It is a second false-flag rate, reported beside C0. It was added before any data and is never dropped if it goes badly.
addendum_2.sharding: batches are grouped by model file and cut into jobs of equal size. The size comes from a seconds-per-batch planning constant in calibration-pins.json; it changes which job runs a batch, never what a batch is, so it is not a method parameter. Every comparison is against the one baseline batch of its own kind.
addendum_2.completeness: the combined report is signed only if every registered batch is present. A missing or UNCHECKABLE batch is reported as such and counted out of the denominator of its condition; a report with a missing batch is not signed.
addendum_2.rates: for each of C0 to C5: flags / comparable trials, exact Wilson 95% interval, mean T, as in section 7. Reading aids: with 0 flags in 30 trials the upper bound is about 0.11 and with 0 in 20 about 0.16; 10 of 10 flags give a lower bound of about 0.72.
addendum_2.second_view: an illustrative CUSUM and Shewhart view of the per-trial T series (measurement/experiments/metrology-controls/check_standard.py). Its reference and spread come from resampling the baseline batch alone, its time axis is the trial order, and it carries no false-alarm rate. It never changes a flag, a rate or the signed payload.
addendum_2.rehearsal: a local run on 2 items and 3 repeats proves the pipeline. Its rows are never published, never signed and never counted; the report refuses any batch marked rehearsal.

runner_limits.source: docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits (the github/docs source file, read 23 Nov 2026); the plan of this repository is unverified, so the matrix runs at most 8 jobs at once

addendum_3.scope: a second calibration run (run 2) with a second decision rule. Sections 1 to 6, the statistic of run 1, the flag rule of run 1, addendum_1 and addendum_2 are unchanged and stay computable; run 1's rule is reported beside the new rule on run 2.
addendum_3.pilot_data_statement: The rows of calibration run 1 (GitHub Actions run 45279396175, signed record sha256 5de64693acd1ae4dce393c28f8cca9505790746031cafc67386e45104c9ade59) were used as PILOT data to choose the rule below (docs/research/silent-change/DIAGNOSIS-RUN1.md). The new rule is judged only on a fresh run (run 2), whose batches do not exist yet. Run 1's signed rates are published as signed and are never re-scored with the new rule.
addendum_3.why: In run 1 every item gave the same answer on all 30 repeats of every batch (1,840 of 1,840 item-batches), so the registered permutation test had no spread to compare against and one moved item gave the smallest possible p. The real variation was between jobs (independent servers): one near-tie item changed its answer from one job to another. The reference for 'no change' must therefore come from repeated independent no-change batches, not from within-batch spread alone.
addendum_3.unit_of_independence: a job: one fresh GitHub-hosted runner and one llama-server start. One job runs exactly one batch. A batch is never run in the same job as a batch it is compared against.

rule_2.name: pooled_baseline_loo_max

baseline_pool.definition: 20 independent no-change batches of the same file and settings, each from its own job

rule_2.pooled_share: for item i and answer category c, s_ic = the mean over the 20 pool batches of that batch's share of c on item i (equal weight per batch; UNPARSED is a category)
rule_2.score: S(x; P) = mean over the 20 items of 0.5 * sum_c |q_ic - s_ic|, where q_ic is batch x's share of c on item i and s is the pooled share of pool P. Same total-variation distance as run 1, with a pooled reference instead of one batch.
rule_2.loo_scores: L_j = S(b_j; P without b_j) for each pool batch b_j, j = 1 to 20 (a baseline batch scored against the other 19)
rule_2.flag: a new batch x is FLAG iff S(x; P) > theta (strictly greater). Ties are NO_FLAG. If theta = 0, any S > 0 is a flag.
rule_2.false_flag_target: at most 1/(N+1) = 1/21 = 0.0476, i.e. about 0.05 per no-change batch, under the assumption that a new no-change batch is exchangeable with the pool batches (same file, same settings, a fresh job). The new batch is scored against 20 pool batches and the pool batches against 19, a small difference that makes the rule slightly conservative; it is not corrected. Whether the target is met is what C0 and C5 of run 2 measure; it is not assumed.
rule_2.no_alpha_no_floor: no p-value, no permutation and no T floor in rule 2; theta comes from the data of the 20 pool batches
reported_with_every_rate: the number of items that moved between pool batches

addendum_3.rule_1_kept: the run 1 rule (within-item permutation test on mean TV, p <= 0.01 and T >= 0.03) is computed on every run 2 trial against the first batch of its pool (BASE-01 for C0 to C4, BASE5-01 for C5) and reported beside rule 2, same conditions, same batches.

BASE.role: the BASE pool; BASE-01 is also the single baseline of rule 1

BASE5.role: the BASE5 pool; BASE5-01 is also the single baseline of rule 1

C3.system: Read the question carefully before answering.

addendum_3.sampling_departure: In run 1 temperature 0.5 gave no spread: the server seed was fixed per shard and all 30 repeats were identical. In run 2, for batches with temperature above 0, each request carries its own seed, an integer from sha256(trial_id, item_id, repeat). Temperature 0 batches are unchanged. This makes C4, C5 and BASE5 sample as a hosted endpoint would; it changes no other setting.
addendum_3.order: the job matrix is a seeded shuffle (seed from sha256 of the protocol id and 'run2-order'), so baseline and trial batches are spread over the whole run in time
recorded_in_every_batch_from_now_on: runner CPU model, logical CPU count, operating system image (ImageOS, ImageVersion), runner name
llama.cpp: the tag, the version line printed by llama-server, and the system_info line of the server log
job: shard name, run id, run attempt
addendum_3.completeness: as in addendum_2: signed only if all 130 batches are present and comparable; a failed job may be re-run in Actions (the same matrix entry); a report with a missing batch is not signed.

expected_false_flag_and_power.basis: a synthetic simulation of rule 2 in the structure the pilot showed (identical answers inside a batch; a few near-tie items that take one of two labels per job with probability one half; changes that move whole items), 20 items, 20 pool batches, 4,000 repetitions per cell. The simulation script is added to the repository after this addendum and must reproduce these numbers. Pilot structure is from 2 to 4 independent jobs per condition, so the number of near-tie items in a 20-job pool is itself unknown.
expected_false_flag_and_power.false_flag: with 0 to 5 near-tie items the simulated false-flag rate is 0.000 to 0.027, below the 0.0476 bound. Target for C0 and C5: at most 0.05. I expect C0 near 0 to 0.05.
expected_false_flag_and_power.C1: expected power 0.9 or more. Why: 2 of 20 items moved in all 10 trials in all 4 jobs of run 1 (T = 0.10), above the 0.025 a single near-tie item contributes; simulated 1.00 with 0 to 5 near-tie items.
expected_false_flag_and_power.C3: expected power 0.9 or more. Why: 3 of 20 items moved in all 10 trials in both jobs (T = 0.15); simulated 1.00.
expected_false_flag_and_power.C2: expected power low, near the false-flag level (0.0 to 0.1). Why: in run 1, Q4_K_M moved no item other than the near-tie item; a rule cannot detect a movement that the 20 items do not show. A small number of flags here would be a finding about the 20 items, not a failure of the rule.
expected_false_flag_and_power.C4: unknown from the pilot, and expected low to moderate. Why: in run 1 temperature 0.5 moved no item beyond the near-tie one, but it was not sampling (fixed seed). With per-request seeds the shares may spread; the pilot says nothing about by how much.
expected_false_flag_and_power.smallest_change: one firm item moving completely (T = 0.05 against a pooled reference of 0): simulated 0.96 to 1.00 with 0 to 5 near-tie items. A shift of a part of one item's answers is smaller and will usually not be seen.
expected_false_flag_and_power.not_claimed: power for any change of a paid model, for any item outside these 20, or for real sampling spread; run 2 measures C0 to C5 and nothing is promised before it.

addendum_3.reporting: for each of C0 to C5 and for each rule: flags / comparable trials, exact Wilson 95% interval, mean S (rule 2) or mean T (rule 1), and for each flag, which items moved. Because trials are in independent jobs, the number of trials equals the number of independent draws. Descriptive only: flags by runner CPU model, with no cause claimed.
addendum_3.second_view: the illustrative CUSUM and Shewhart view (check_standard.py) takes its reference and spread from the 20 L_j of the pool instead of from resampling one batch; it changes no flag, rate or signed payload.
addendum_3.rehearsal: a local run on a tiny slice proves the pipeline; its rows are never published, signed or counted.
addendum_3.still_true: A flag is a detected change in answer behaviour on the probe items. It is not a cause. Nothing here makes a claim about any paid model. Measurement, not certification.
